declarations.description:
The frame of an application: a banner, a header, a navigation, the main content, an optional aside (a details panel)
and a footer, each in its own slot and landmark, plus a built-in skip link to main.

The layout follows the shell's **own width**, not the window's, so the same markup behaves inside an iframe, a split
view or a docs example frame. Below 600px the navigation is a modal drawer (`over`); from 600px `tablet-mode` and from
960px `desktop-mode` choose between `side` (pushes main), `rail` (collapses to its icons; expanded it pushes) and
`over`. The aside is a column from 960px and a sheet from the end edge below that. Container queries draw the
layout, so the server-rendered first paint is already right.

Put a `c2-app-shell-toggle` (or any element with `app-shell-toggle="navigation"` / `"aside"`) anywhere inside the
shell, including inside the slotted `c2-header`, to open and close the navigation or the aside with no script. With
the drawer open, focus moves into it and stays there, Escape and the backdrop close it, and focus returns to the
toggle. In a collapsed rail, hide the item labels with
`c2-app-shell:state(rail):not(:state(navigation-opened)) .label { display: none }`.

With `scrolling="page"` (default) the page scrolls and the header region sticks to the top; with `scrolling="main"` the
shell takes `--c2-app-shell--height` and only main scrolls. Either way the shell sets
`--c2-app-shell--sticky-offset` to the height that sticky content in main must clear, which `c2-page-header` reads.
declarations.name: AppShell

members.name: layout
members.description: `header-first`: the header spans the width. `navigation-first`: the navigation runs the full height and the header sits above main.

members.name: navigationOpened
members.description:
Whether the navigation is open: the side panel shown, the rail expanded, the drawer open. The shell changes it
itself when its width changes, so it does not reflect; style the live state with `:state(navigation-opened)`.
Below 600px the initial value is ignored and the drawer starts closed.

members.name: desktopMode
members.description: Presentation of the navigation at 960px of width and up.

members.name: tabletMode
members.description: Presentation of the navigation from 600px to 959px. Below 600px it is always `over`.

members.name: asideOpened
members.description: Whether the aside is shown: a column from 960px, a sheet below. Does not reflect; style it with `:state(aside-opened)`.

members.name: scrolling
members.description: `page`: the page scrolls and the header sticks. `main`: the shell takes `--c2-app-shell--height` and only main scrolls.

members.name: closeOnNavigate
members.description: In `over` mode, a click on a link inside the navigation closes the drawer and moves focus to main.

members.name: navigationLabel
members.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Empty: "Main" in the page language.

members.name: asideLabel
members.description: Accessible name of the aside landmark, for slotted content that does not name itself.

members.name: storageKey
members.description: When set, the user's choice to expand or collapse a `side` or `rail` navigation is kept in `localStorage` under this key.

members.name: preferred
members.description: The open state the user last chose for `side` and `rail`, restored when the width comes back to that mode.

members.name: authorOpened
members.description: `navigationOpened` as the author set it before the first measurement; undefined when they left it alone.

members.name: restored
members.description: The modes whose open state came from `storage-key`.

members.name: navigationDrawer
members.default: new DrawerController(this, { panel: () => this.navigationElement, slots: () => this.slotsIn(this.navigationElement), onEscape: () => this.setNavigation(false), })

members.name: asideDrawer
members.default: new DrawerController(this, { panel: () => this.asideElement, slots: () => this.slotsIn(this.asideElement), onEscape: () => this.setAside(false), })

members.name: breakpoint
members.description: The shell's width class: `phone` below 600px, `tablet` to 959px, `desktop` from 960px.

members.name: mode
members.description: The presentation of the navigation in effect for the current width.

members.name: toggleNavigation
members.description: Opens or closes the navigation as a user action would (fires `navigation-opened-change`).

members.name: toggleAside
members.description: Opens or closes the aside as a user action would (fires `aside-opened-change`).

members.name: focusMain
members.description: Moves focus to the start of main, as the skip link does.

members.name: applyMode
members.description: Puts the navigation (and a sheet aside) in the default state of the mode in effect, after a width or mode change.

events.name: mode-change
events.description: The shell's width crossed 600px or 960px, or a mode attribute changed the presentation in effect. Does not bubble.

events.name: navigation-opened-change
events.description: The user (a toggle, the backdrop, Escape, a link with `close-on-navigate`) or a width change opened or closed the navigation. Not fired when `navigationOpened` is set from code. Does not bubble.

events.name: aside-opened-change
events.description: The user or a width change opened or closed the aside. Not fired when `asideOpened` is set from code. Does not bubble.

declarations.description:
The button that opens and closes the navigation (or the aside) of the enclosing `c2-app-shell`. It finds its shell
through a context, so it works anywhere inside it, including inside a slotted `c2-header`, with no id and no script.
Its `aria-expanded` and its name follow the shell ("Open navigation" / "Close navigation"), and its default icon is a
menu glyph while the navigation is a drawer and a sidebar glyph beside main. Outside a shell it renders nothing.
declarations.name: AppShellToggle

members.name: for
members.description: What the button opens: the shell's `navigation` or its `aside`.

members.name: label
members.description: Accessible name. Empty: "Open navigation" / "Close navigation" (or "Show details" / "Close details") in the page language.

members.name: consumer
members.default: new ContextConsumer(this, { context: appShellContext, subscribe: true })

members.name: hydrated
members.description:
False for the first render, on the server and in the browser alike: a server renderer has no shell to ask, and
hydration keeps the attributes the server wrote, so the first client render must match it.
